objects.title: Family caregivers underuse relief services; counselors cite refusal, self-reliance and information gaps
objects.statement: Two distinct survey populations point to underuse of relief services. In the pflege.de 2025 caregiver self-report survey, only 6% of surveyed family caregivers regularly use Pflegekassen offers (Pflegeberatung, Pflegekurse, Entlastungsleistungen); cited reasons: not knowing they exist or no time (37%), bureaucratic effort (35%), offers unhelpful (24%). In the separate Diakonie counselor survey, counselors most often name as barriers to caregivers' use of support: care recipient refusing outside help (86.75%), wish to manage alone (68.37%), unknown suitable offers (43.99%), unavailable offers or long wait times (42.05%), reluctance to ask family/friends (35.87%), too-low Pflegegrad (18.9%); free-text answers add bureaucratic obstacles, access problems, shame/pride/social pressure, and high organizational effort vs. low expected relief.

scope.limitations: pflege.de survey summary lacks exact sample size/recruitment; commercial portal. Diakonie survey is counselor-reported (secondary perspective); percentages are counselor assessments, not caregiver prevalence. The same Diakonie source gives conflicting values for the financial barrier (84.10% in one passage vs 68.37% reported elsewhere for the same item), so the financial percentage is omitted here pending clarification. Exact questionnaire wording unknown.
scope.methodology: Caregiver self-report survey (pflege.de 2025) and provider-workflow survey of Diakonie care counselors (2025)
scope.stakeholders: Family caregivers, care recipients, care counselors

confidence.rationale: Two distinct respondent perspectives report barriers; their populations and limitations remain separate. Candidate status retains limits and the financial discrepancy.

objects.title: High caregiver burden and health toll reported from both counselor and caregiver perspectives
objects.statement: High caregiver burden is reported from two separate populations. Diakonie counselors rate as frequent burdens among caregiver clients: emotional strain (74.73%), psychological strain (67.80%), being time-bound (56.89%), physical strain (50.72%), health problems (45.41%), lack of private life (43.88%), lack of support from other family members (35.14%), decline of social contacts (34.99%), work-care incompatibility (31.63%). In the pflege.de caregiver self-report survey, 96% of surveyed caregivers report more frequent health complaints in the last six months (for 7 in 10 these first appeared during caregiving; only 4% still rate their health 'very good'); about one third report social isolation, many report guilt about taking care breaks (not quantified), and 33% have no one to step in if they fall ill — only 10% feel prepared for that case.

scope.limitations: Counselor-reported burdens (Diakonie) vs caregiver self-report (pflege.de) are separate populations; pflege.de sample size unknown; no causal attribution of health complaints to caregiving alone; guilt about care breaks is reported qualitatively ('viele berichten') without a quantified denominator.

scope.stakeholders: Family caregivers, care recipients

objects.title: Official access conditions: Entlastungsbetrag €131/month reimbursement (BMG)
objects.statement: Official BMG documentation of an existing public relief mechanism: care recipients in home care (including Pflegegrad 1) are entitled to an Entlastungsbetrag of up to €131/month (up to €1,572/year), purpose-bound to quality-assured relief services for caregivers and to Landesrecht-anerkannte Angebote zur Unterstützung im Alltag; unused monthly amounts carry over, and amounts unused at year's end can be carried forward until the end of the following calendar half-year. Reimbursement requires submitting receipts and a reimbursement application to the Pflegekasse identifying the services to which the costs relate and the amount claimed.

scope.limitations: Official description of entitlement and access procedure; no data on actual uptake or whether the process works smoothly in practice. Page undated in capture.

objects.statement: In the ZipA survey (n=1,429 caregivers, Nov 2018–Mar 2019), 70% felt strongly burdened, 72% psychologically strained, 75% restricted in leisure/social life, 68% in privacy, about half physically overworked, and 42% rated their health worse than peers. evidence_links.excerpt: Viele der Befragten fühlen sich durch die Pflege stark belastet (70 %). So begnügten sich einige Studienteilnehmer und -teilnehmerinnen nicht mit dem Ausfüllen des Fragebogens, sondern kontaktierten die Forscherinnen und berichteten teilweise sehr emotional, wie allein gelassen sie sich mit ihren Sorgen und Anliegen fühlen. Fast die Hälfte fühlt sich durch die Pflege körperlich überfordert und leidet gesundheitlich. Im Vergleich zu Gleichaltrigen schätzen 42 % ihren Gesundheitszustand als schlechter ein. record.title: High caregiver burden and health toll reported from both counselor and caregiver perspectives
record.statement: High caregiver burden is reported from two separate populations. Diakonie counselors rate as frequent burdens among caregiver clients: emotional strain (74.73%), psychological strain (67.80%), being time-bound (56.89%), physical strain (50.72%), health problems (45.41%), lack of private life (43.88%), lack of support from other family members (35.14%), decline of social contacts (34.99%), work-care incompatibility (31.63%). In the pflege.de caregiver self-report survey, 96% of surveyed caregivers report more frequent health complaints in the last six months (for 7 in 10 these first appeared during caregiving; only 4% still rate their health 'very good'); about one third report social isolation, many report guilt about taking care breaks (not quantified), and 33% have no one to step in if they fall ill — only 10% feel prepared for that case.

Angesichts der unübersichtlichen Informationslage wird es den ärztlichen Teams nicht leicht gemacht, einen Überblick zu Informations- und Beratungsangeboten in der Region zu geben und auf diese, wie in der Leitlinie empfohlen, zu verweisen.

record.excerpt: Viele der Befragten fühlen sich durch die Pflege stark belastet (70 %). So begnügten sich einige Studienteilnehmer und -teilnehmerinnen nicht mit dem Ausfüllen des Fragebogens, sondern kontaktierten die Forscherinnen und berichteten teilweise sehr emotional, wie allein gelassen sie sich mit ihren Sorgen und Anliegen fühlen. Fast die Hälfte fühlt sich durch die Pflege körperlich überfordert und leidet gesundheitlich. Im Vergleich zu Gleichaltrigen schätzen 42 % ihren Gesundheitszustand als schlechter ein. Vor allem aber verursacht die Angehörigenpflege emotionale Belastung. So fühlen sich 72 % der Befragten psychisch stark belastet. Angehörige sehen sich darüber hinaus in ihrer Privatsphäre (68 %) sowie in ihren Freizeitaktivitäten und in ihrem Sozialleben (75 %) eingeschränkt. Die Unterstützung bei Pflegebedürftigkeit hat auch Einfluss auf berufliche Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten. So sehen sich mehr als 30 % der Befragten bei der Suche nach einer Arbeitsstelle benachteiligt und mehr als 20 % der Berufstätigen berichten, dass ihre Arbeitsleistung durch die Angehörigenpflege beeinträchtigt wird.

record.title: Family caregivers underuse relief services; counselors cite refusal, self-reliance and information gaps
record.statement: Two distinct survey populations point to underuse of relief services. In the pflege.de 2025 caregiver self-report survey, only 6% of surveyed family caregivers regularly use Pflegekassen offers (Pflegeberatung, Pflegekurse, Entlastungsleistungen); cited reasons: not knowing they exist or no time (37%), bureaucratic effort (35%), offers unhelpful (24%). In the separate Diakonie counselor survey, counselors most often name as barriers to caregivers' use of support: care recipient refusing outside help (86.75%), wish to manage alone (68.37%), unknown suitable offers (43.99%), unavailable offers or long wait times (42.05%), reluctance to ask family/friends (35.87%), too-low Pflegegrad (18.9%); free-text answers add bureaucratic obstacles, access problems, shame/pride/social pressure, and high organizational effort vs. low expected relief.

confidence.rationale: Two distinct respondent perspectives report barriers; their populations and limitations remain separate. Candidate status retains limits and the financial discrepancy.
